Survey items 1 and 10 (outside_research/research_01_survey.md) both carry the note 'Dựa theo nguồn 100%, không tự generate thông tin mới' (base 100% on source, never self-generate) -- the exact principle this validator enforces mechanically: every claim in the 3 grounded sections (verified facts, statutory grounds, application analysis) must cite a real, caller-declared source, and a citation to a nonexistent source id is a hard error. Same discipline already applied by citation-management to academic citations, extended here to legal research given Stanford RegLab/HAI's 'Hallucination-Free?' finding that even purpose-built legal-AI tools hallucinate 17-33% of the time (docs/specs/STRATEGY_SPEC.md §5.2).

skills.elicited_from: Elicited from survey item 6 (outside_research/research_01_survey.md: contract risk review, flagging unfavorable clauses, proposing amendments). Deliberately does NOT attempt automated risk detection -- identifying a clause as risky requires legal judgment this project does not automate. Structured instead as a completeness/consistency validator over a human-or-agent-authored risk log, mirroring this repo's peer-review claim-evidence-matrix pattern (validate structure of analysis, not the analysis itself). The explicit-not-ambiguous no-issues-found requirement is new to this skill: a silently-empty issues list in a legal risk log is a genuinely dangerous ambiguity between 'reviewed, clean' and 'not reviewed.'
